title: Editable web capture and native import

nodes.title: Browser capture contract
nodes.detail: The read-only page evaluation exports visible text, geometry, supported vector and control structure, local image request references, and explicit limitations. It does not read input values, cookies, or storage.

nodes.title: Capture rendered web screens as bounded observations
nodes.detail: Capture visible browser content into stable screen and element records while retaining the viewport, observed text and styles, ancestor paths, and unsupported-content limitations.

nodes.title: Bind local images to exact bytes
nodes.detail: Bind only explicit root-relative local image requests to files whose declared MIME type, byte signature, and SHA-256 match.

nodes.title: Prepare and verify editable native screens
nodes.detail: Validate the selected screen graph, pin its source hash, and apply it through the existing native-edit path with bounded geometry and asset inputs.

nodes.title: Reuse a component only when observed text metrics match
nodes.detail: Component identity and imported instance readback must preserve captured typography and layout metrics such as line height.

nodes.title: Record observed page geometry and content without unbounded browser data
nodes.detail: Four local template pages were captured into versioned graphs. Their element counts, measured document extents, and reported limitations are listed in the linked verification record.

nodes.title: Use only explicitly pinned local image bytes in native preparation
nodes.detail: Eight Portfolio photos and three Devtool thumbnails passed byte-hash, signature, native IMAGE fill, and decoded-size checks. Four final Figma previews were visually compared with the browser outputs. Three external Portfolio SVGs were excluded.

nodes.title: Create editable native frames from four captured templates
nodes.detail: Final shipping apply/readback receipts report 512, 526, 41, and 23 editable nodes, 1102 total, excluding VECTOR descendants. The result covers these four observed inputs, not general website support or pixel parity.

nodes.title: Create editable native frames from the initial four template graphs
nodes.detail: The initial pass reported 510, 462, 40, and 23 editable nodes, 1035 total. This verifies the initial inputs, not visual parity or general website support.

nodes.title: Preserve user edits when reapplying unchanged graphs
nodes.detail: All four shipping graph IDs reapplied without changes. On SaaS, changing the main button font from 14 to 16 was preserved by an intervening same-graph apply; restoring 14 allowed a final apply with no write.

nodes.title: Preserve measured line height through native component reuse
nodes.detail: Three browser buttons with line heights 20, 24, and 20 pixels produced two mains and one instance. All native line heights matched, and repeat apply made no changes.

nodes.title: Read-only browser page capture
nodes.detail: Exports bounded visible DOM observations and flags unsupported visual content.

nodes.title: Bind captures into a graph
nodes.detail: Combines capture records and explicit local image bindings into a versioned graph.

nodes.title: Validate and pin a native import plan
nodes.detail: Validates screen IDs, geometry, SVG, image hashes, source freshness, and bounded raster embedding.

nodes.title: Create and read back native web screens
nodes.detail: Builds editable native nodes, checks the imported scene against its owned frame, and returns per-screen counts.

nodes.title: Portfolio editable native frame
nodes.detail: Final shipping receipt reports 512 editable nodes, including 2 instances. The frame identifier is retained only in private local evidence.

nodes.title: Codeforge editable native frame
nodes.detail: Final shipping receipt reports 526 editable nodes, including 24 instances. The frame identifier is retained only in private local evidence.

nodes.title: Devtool editable native frame
nodes.detail: Final shipping receipt reports 41 editable nodes, including 1 instance. Twenty-one GeistSans font aliases resolved to Geist Regular, Bold, or SemiBold; fallback notices report the family alias. The frame identifier is retained only in private local evidence.

nodes.title: SaaS signup editable native frame
nodes.detail: Final shipping receipt reports 23 editable nodes. The frame identifier is retained only in private local evidence.

nodes.title: Web graph validation and import checks
nodes.detail: Focused web tests passed (eight Python and four native bridge Node). The stable-clone release suite passed 1215 Python, 326 Node, 75 finalize, 18 design, and 2 demo tests, all with zero skips. The final three Node cases cover component identity, instance typography readback, and mismatch rollback.

nodes.title: Actual native apply and readback for four templates
nodes.detail: Four shipping apply/readback receipts report successful completion and the editable-node counts recorded above.

nodes.title: Image byte and native gradient verification
nodes.detail: Eight Portfolio photos and three Devtool thumbnails passed native image hash, signature, and decoded-size checks. Four Figma previews were visually compared with browser output. Four Codeforge native radial fills were verified.

nodes.title: Reapply and conflict protection for unchanged graphs
nodes.detail: Four stable screen IDs produced no-op reapply results. The SaaS font-size edit was preserved during a conflicting apply and restored before an unchanged reapply.

nodes.title: Line-height component separation and readback check
nodes.detail: The native bridge suite verifies different line heights produce distinct mains and rejects an instance whose text metrics differ from the capture.

nodes.title: Actual browser capture of four template pages
nodes.detail: Four captured screen graphs retain document dimensions, element counts, and limitations.

nodes.title: Preserve computed CSS letter spacing
nodes.detail: Capture numeric computed CSS letter-spacing in pixels as optional text.letterSpacing. Omit normal values. Keep the value pinned through graph validation and native planning. Include tracking in component ownership, then compare native PIXELS range values when reading mains and instances.

nodes.title: Retain optional letter spacing in the graph and native plan
nodes.detail: The focused Python test asserts that -1.12 px survives graph validation and native plan creation, and that normal tracking remains omitted.

nodes.title: Read back captured letter spacing from native component text
nodes.detail: On a four-button browser capture, actual Figma getters returned +1.5 px and -0.75 px. Repeated imports retained both main IDs and linked each instance to the main with matching tracking.

nodes.title: Return a bounded raster preview after native import
nodes.detail: Warm the first PNG export for a new image-backed screen or video poster fallback, discard those bytes, and return the second export. Bound export time, pixel dimensions, and the private preview-byte total.

nodes.title: Return valid raster preview bytes within native export limits
nodes.detail: Record the first-export warm-up and fallback rules, the 45-second export timeout, the 5,000,000-pixel ceiling, the 8 MB total preview limit, and actual native preview evidence.

nodes.title: Optional tracking through graph validation and native planning
nodes.detail: The focused Python test covers nonzero CSS pixels through the graph and native plan, plus omission for normal tracking.

nodes.title: First raster export warm-up policy
nodes.detail: The focused Node test checks that new image-backed screens return the second export, while reused or vector-only screens export once. It also covers video fallback policy.

nodes.title: Compare a browser graph with native text ranges and instance main IDs
Preserve supported color filters on external SVG images
nodes.detail: Capture bounded color filter operations for external SVG images. When brightness(0) makes the filtered RGB color independent of the source paint, recolor literal SVG fills and strokes while retaining alpha and separate element opacity. Preserve source vectors and report a limitation when the filter or paint cannot be transformed safely.

nodes.title: Match the six Devtool logos' browser monochrome treatment
nodes.detail: All six source SVGs remained pinned in bound_media; none was omitted or raster-fallbacked. Their subtrees contain 26 editable VECTOR descendants. In measured logo boxes, pixels whose RGB channel range exceeded 40 fell from 4,308 in the 0.32.1 first output to zero in the 0.32.2 first output, matching the browser count. The Google layer's native opacity readback was 30 percent. First apply and reapply reused the same Figma frame. The 480 by 1,052 preview was 73,070 bytes, within the 5,000,000-pixel and 8 MB limits.

nodes.title: Capture exact supported SVG image filter operations
nodes.detail: The browser capture test retains brightness(0), grayscale(1), invert(1), the computed silhouette color, and the separate 0.3 image opacity.

nodes.title: Recolor supported SVG paints and retain encoded alpha
nodes.detail: The media binding test verifies monochrome literal fills and strokes, preserved encoded alpha, the filter data, and the image opacity.

nodes.title: Keep unsupported filtered source vectors visible
nodes.detail: The binder keeps an SVG that uses currentColor in its original colors and records the unsupported-filter limitation instead of omitting the image.

nodes.title: Bound captured SVG filter-chain metadata
nodes.detail: A 17-operation chain remains visible, has no claimed silhouette transform, and reports the unsupported filter limitation.

nodes.title: Keep element opacity separate from SVG group opacity
nodes.detail: The native vector test applies the captured element opacity to the vector root without changing SVG child paint or the SVG group's own opacity.
